papers.title: UNCEMENTED PRIMARY TOTAL HIP ARTHROPLASTY FOR OSTEONECROSIS OF HIP WITH SECONDARY OSTEOARTHRITIS IN YOUNG ADULTS
papers.abstract: Osteonecrosis of the femoral head is a progressive disease that generally affects patients in the third through fifth decade of life, if left untreated. Currently, 18% of all Total Hip Arthroplasty performed in USA are done for Osteonecrosis. The aetiology for the Osteonecrosis varies from idiopathic, alcohol intoxication, steroid abuse or due to childhood hip disorders and hip trauma. We have selected 40 patients suffering from advanced femoral head osteonecrosis with subchondral collapse leading to Osteoarthritis of hip in young adults, treated by uncemented primary total hip replacement. This study is aimed to suggest that uncemented total hip arthroplasty can be applied predictably to this younger, potentially more active patient population.

summary_en.motivation: To assess clinical outcomes of uncemented total hip arthroplasty in young adults with femoral head osteonecrosis.
summary_en.method: 40 patients with advanced osteonecrosis and secondary osteoarthritis underwent uncemented primary total hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.result: Uncemented total hip arthroplasty can be reliably applied to a younger, more active patient population.
